subject: Literature
title: The Qin Dynasty Book Burning
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Qin Dynasty Book Burning.

hook.text: In 213 BC, China's first emperor ordered all books burned except those about medicine, farming, and divination.

buildup.text: Emperor Qin Shi Huang wanted to erase history before his dynasty so his rule would seem like the true beginning.

discovery.text: Scholars who resisted were buried alive, and hundreds of Confucian texts were lost in the campaign.

twist.text: Some scholars hid texts in walls and caves, and fragments were recovered centuries later during construction.

climax.text: The Qin burning showed that erasing the past is often the first act of any regime trying to control the future.

punchline.text: He burned history, but history remembered what he did.

quiz.question: Why did Qin Shi Huang order books burned?
options: To save paper for military records
To erase history before his dynasty so his rule seemed like the beginning
To punish a specific group of authors
